ig_carousel_topic.topic: Bankroll math for people who've never thought about bankroll
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
You don't need a system.
You need a number.
Bankroll math, from scratch.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
Most bettors skip this part.
They pick a bet size by feel, $50 here, $200 there, and wonder why a bad week wipes them out.
The problem isn't the picks. It's the sizing.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
Flat-unit betting is the fix.
Pick a unit size: 1% to 2% of your total bankroll.
Bet that amount on every play, regardless of how confident you feel.
A $500 bankroll means $5 to $10 per bet. That's it.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Say your bankroll is $1,000. Your unit is $10 (1%).
You go 5-5 over 10 bets at -110 juice.
5 wins: +$45.45. 5 losses: -$50. Net: -$4.55.
You're still in the game. A $100 flat bet? Same record wipes $45.50 from a $1,000 roll.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
A 54% win rate at 1-unit flat betting compounds quietly over hundreds of bets.
The math only works if you're still in action on bet 300.
Size small. Stay in.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: Bankroll sizing is the part most bettors skip. One bad week shouldn't end the run. The math is simple once you see it.
